history.summary: A 1,163 sqft 3BR at Regent Grove (Yew Tee, 99yr from 1997, 70yr left) asking $1.18M / $1,015 psf after a real $70k cut from $1.25M. The MMR's 822 rests almost entirely on a -20.3% gap to the age-adjusted D23 median, but that gap is the permanent Yew Tee/CCK price level, not a dislocation: against the project's own 23 same-size URA prints of the last 24 months (median $1,002 psf; 12-month median $997) the ask is a ~2% PREMIUM, not a discount. What is left is an ordinary, fairly-priced OCR leasehold with one genuine edge - 360m to Yew Tee NS5 - and a project whose own median PSF has been flat for two years. Neutral.
history.rating_rationale: The single largest MMR component (age_value +14.63 of the ~+55 total lift) is a sub-market composition artifact. The $1,274 age-adjusted D23 benchmark is set by Bukit Panjang/Upper Bukit Timah stock and D23 new launches at ~$2,080 psf; Regent Grove's own median has been $1,021-$1,034 psf since 2025 and has never approached it. The gap has not closed and is not closing - it is a location level. Priced against its own market the ask is fair, not cheap: 23 tight same-size prints (1,082-1,244 sqft, 24mo) run min $870 / median $1,002 / max $1,101, and the last 12 months (n=11) median $997 - so $1,015 psf sits at roughly the 64th percentile of its own cohort. An independent portal read of the same book (12-month range $870-$1,156, average $1,008 psf) corroborates it. Split by floor the 11-15 band clears ~$1,040 and the 01-05 band ~$997; the listing carries no floor, no stack and Regent Grove has no researched profile, so the unit could be a ~2% discount (high floor) or a ~2-5% premium (low/mid) - unknown floor means no discount can be credited. The price cut is real (same listing id 500150574, same agent, $1.25M 7 Jun -> $1.18M 28 Jul, relisted 27 Jul), not the unit_group chaining artifact - but it moved an aspirational ask down to market, which is realism rather than value; the five sibling 3BR listings at $1,080-$1,118 psf all sit above every 2026 print. On the other side the positives are real but ordinary: 360m to Yew Tee NS5 (the strongest as-of-today lever here), OCR region (+3.7%/yr realized forward, the best region in the panel), deep liquidity (553 units, 1,235 lifetime transactions, 23 same-size prints in 24 months, 76% HDB buyers), 4.07% gross / 2.45% net yield on a verified $4,000 median rent, and age 26 sits inside the 7-30yr forward-return plateau. Against them: the trailing 5.77%/yr is a spent 2021-26 OCR re-rating (project median $714 psf in 2021 -> $1,021 in 2026) that has already stopped - 2025 $1,034 -> 2026 $1,021 is -1.3%, and the scorer's own momentum reads -1.0, so the ROI table's 6.1%/yr and $1.54M five-year exit are not a credible base case. realsmart REALSCORE is a middling 3.7/5 on a deep sample where 146 of 685 computable exits (21%) sold at a loss, with 8.9yrs average holding against the 5-7yr window underwritten here. Lease is 70yr now, ~64 at exit - not yet at the CPF cliff but starting to shorten the next buyer's runway. Strip the district-relative artifact and this scores a little above market-typical on MRT, liquidity and carry, with no verified entry discount and a plateaued price series. That is a Neutral - a sound, liquid, fairly-priced unit, not an edge.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Genuinely solid and well-evidenced. 45 rental contracts recorded in the past month with a $4,000 median for 3BR in the 1,100-1,200 sqft band (range $3,900-$4,950), giving 4.07% gross / 2.45% net on this ask - realsmart's independent 4.2% estimate corroborates it. Yew Tee at 360m plus the Sungei Kadut / Kranji industrial belt and Woodlands corridor sustain a steady mid-market tenant pool, and a 3-bed/3-bath 1,163 sqft layout co-shares well. But the rent band is tight and flat ($3,900-$4,000 across five of the last six contracts), so treat this as stable carry, not growing income - and per the backtest, a yield this healthy is mildly negative for forward capital growth, not supportive of it.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The trailing 5.77%/yr on 97 transactions is real history and entirely spent. Project median PSF ran $671 (2019) -> $714 (2021) -> $1,021 (2026), but essentially all of that was the 2021-26 OCR re-rating, and it has stopped: 2025 median $1,034 -> 2026 $1,021 (-1.3%) on 18 then 12 sales, with the scorer's momentum at its floor (-1.0) and 2026 prints scattered $870-$1,058. Forward, this is an ordinary OCR leasehold with no entry discount to work with, no dated catalyst (Choa Chu Kang JRL is 1.6km - and future-infra has no measured forward power anyway), and Tengah plus the D23 launch pipeline competing for its HDB-upgrader pool. I anchor the forward rate to the backtested realized OCR baseline of +3.7%/yr rather than the trailing figure; a 5-7yr exit near $1,150-$1,200 psf is the honest central case, versus the $1,322 psf the ROI table implies. Lease decay from 70 to ~64 years works quietly against even that.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Nothing is known about this unit's position. Regent Grove has no researched profile (stack_profile: not_researched), the listing carries no floor or stack, and the DB floor_level is null. This matters more than usual here because the project's own prints split cleanly by floor: over the last 12 months the 11-15 band cleared ~$1,040 psf ($996, $1,039, $1,040, $1,058) while the 01-05 band cleared ~$997 ($870, $963, $997, $1,002, $1,075). The $1,015 ask sits between the two clusters, so a high floor would make it a ~2% discount and a low or mid floor a ~2-5% premium. No trust flag fired (no ask_above_own_stack_prints, no ask_below_stack_prints, stack_low_floor_share not triggered) and the 1,163 sqft is verified real by 11 URA prints at 1,162.51 sqft, so this is not a mis-scrape or a PES/loft artifact - simply an undisclosed floor. Confirm the floor, facing (blocks front Choa Chu Kang North 7 and the internal grounds) and renovation condition before any offer; that single fact decides whether this ask is fair or slightly rich.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Resale-to-resale, project's own URA prints: Regent Grove is 100% resale stock (2000 completion) and its own median PSF has plateaued - 2025 $1,034 -> 2026 $1,021 (-1.3%), with the tight same-size 12-month median ($997, n=11) at/below the 24-month median ($1,002, n=23). The trailing 5.77%/yr 5-year CAGR is the spent 2021-26 OCR re-rating and per the backtest carries ~0 forward power, so I anchor instead to the measured realized OCR forward baseline of +3.7%/yr. No dated catalyst justifies a premium to it (JRL Choa Chu Kang is 1.6km and future-infra has no measured forward power).
